intro: Art is where I find my voice. I paint the quiet moments we often miss, from the light on an ancient temple wall to the unguarded look on a face, in watercolour, graphite, ink and pastel.

bio: I grew up in a coastal village in Bagerhat, Bangladesh, where the tides and old traditions first taught me how to pay attention. My days are mostly consumed by engineering, building AI systems and robotics, but painting is my native language.
Heavily influenced by Sanatani heritage and South Asian art, I paint the quiet moments people usually walk right past: the weight of the light on a temple wall, a face caught entirely off guard.

My canvases live somewhere between the ancient and the automated. I find myself returning to divine figures and old architecture to ground myself, and then drifting forward to sketch imagined worlds of machines and the people intertwined with them. To me, a river at dawn or a quick concept sketch of a mechanical joint are just different ways of telling the truth.

Over the years, this work has earned more than 40 awards, including recognition from the Bangladesh Shishu Academy and the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy. My pieces have been shown in three exhibitions, one of which allowed me to share the art of my hometown with delegates from the United Nations.

artworks.title: The Potter’s Hands
artworks.description: Haripada never looks at the wheel; his gaze wanders past the doorway of his shed in Kagajipara while his thumbs patiently interrogate the obedient clay. Every true craft, I suspect, is a colloquy with a substance far older than ourselves, and mastery is merely the hard-won humility to stop interrupting it.

artworks.title: The Devotee
artworks.description: Devotion, I believe, is less supplication than sanctuary. Amid the clamour of drums and incense, the faithful are not petitioning the divine so much as hollowing out a numinous quietude within themselves, a cloister where the world's din is finally rendered small.

artworks.title: Life on the Water
artworks.description: At Sadarghat no vessel ever truly arrives; each merely jostles the next aside. A river city, I came to realise, is not founded upon land at all, but upon ten thousand ephemeral covenants struck between strangers, hour after hour, across restless water.

artworks.title: Steps of Ancients
artworks.description: On the Dashashwamedh steps, every stone is hollowed at its centre by countless bare feet. Faith resides not in the spires but in that slow erosion, the palimpsest a single footfall, repeated across a millennium, inscribes upon unyielding stone.

artworks.title: Sci-Fi Characters
artworks.medium: Fine-liner ink and pen on paper
artworks.description: I distrust visions of a gleaming, immaculate tomorrow. The future, I suspect, will be a bricolage of salvage: patched, cannibalised, inherited, held together by the obstinate ingenuity of people too stubborn to await deliverance. These ragged wanderers are my small heresy against utopia.

artworks.title: Whispers of Buddha
artworks.description: Perhaps, after all, enlightenment is not an illumination that descends upon us, but a shadow that finally ceases to follow us home, the quiet dissolution of the self until even one's own name grows faint and evanescent.

artworks.title: The Tandava of Lord Shiva
artworks.description: In the Tandava, annihilation and genesis are a single choreography; the very step that unmakes one cosmos inaugurates the next. Nothing, I think, is ever truly obliterated. It is merely transfigured, danced, with terrible tenderness, into another incarnation of form.

artworks.title: The Quiet Table
artworks.description: The fruit will be devoured by dusk and the wine drained before the light shifts, which is precisely why it deserves preserving. A still life is a quiet insurrection against transience, an insistence that the ordinary once warranted unhurried attention. Most of existence unfolds in such unremarkable interludes, too mundane for anyone to notice, and evanescent before we think to look.

artworks.title: The Studio Sanctuary
artworks.description: The artist presumes himself the sole observer, yet the courtyard is forever composing its own canvas, vine by vine, across crumbling masonry. Every painter is watched in return by something more patient than himself, something sure to outlast the work.

artworks.title: Human Figures
artworks.description: The body is never truly still. Even in repose it labours beneath its own gravity, negotiating weight and strain with a stoic, unheralded grace. To draw the figure is to witness that silent exertion, the dignity concealed within mere existence.

artworks.title: The Pensive Sari
artworks.description: The most sequestered chamber a person possesses has no threshold at all. We simply recede into it mid-sentence, amid a garden or a crowd, and quietly vanish. Portraiture, at its finest, is the futile and beautiful attempt to follow.

artworks.title: Indigo Morning
artworks.description: Before dawn on the Bhairab, the fishermen of Bagerhat keep silent, for voices travel too far across still water. As a child, I imagined the fog concealed the far bank. Now I believe it was merciful, allowing each new day to commence before we could reckon how far still remained.

artworks.title: Shade and Blossom
artworks.description: In the old miniatures, a woman beneath a tree is never merely at rest; she awaits something that the painter deliberately withholds. I have long cherished that reticence. An image that refuses its denouement compels us to linger a while longer, to supply the ending ourselves, and so to become accomplices in its making.

artworks.title: Lines of a Lifetime
artworks.description: Abdul Karim planted every tree in his village twice: once in youth, and once after the cyclone of 1991. I did not draw wrinkles. I drew the attrition of rebuilding, the years inscribed line upon line until his countenance could no longer tell them apart.

artworks.title: The Waiting Boat
artworks.description: Boats, I think, understand patience better than we do. They are fashioned to idle between voyages, and nobody condemns their waiting as squandered. Perhaps we owe ourselves that same tender clemency on our fallow days, when nothing arrives and the river merely continues to hold its breath.

artworks.title: Beneath the Trees
artworks.description: Certain friendships grow so burnished by the years that conversation would only scratch their surface. Companionship at its most profound is a shared, unspoken cadence, like the ancient trees that have known one another for centuries and confer in nothing but shade.
